newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - May 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - May 30.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Friday:
* Cash investments in mutual funds have gained strength in the past two months.
* Nike Inc stock plunged after the company offered a grim forecast for its quarterly earnings.
* Scholastic Corp offered a series of cost cuts, including the elimination of 400 jobs.
* The advertising agency of Bozell, Jacobs, Kenyon & Eckhardt is being pursued by two suitors: Omnicom Group Inc and True North Communications Inc.
* Toy Biz Inc has backed away from an agreement with Marvel Entertainment Group Inc bondholders, who are seeking control.
* Securities regulators from 20 states have filed lawsuits and taken other action against stockbrokers who push penny stocks by telephone.
* Boston Chicken Inc said it was not satisfied with sales at its Boston Market Stores, and that the head of the unit has resigned.
* Esquire has named David Granger editor in chief of the magazine.
* Sybase Inc's executive vice president of product development left this month to become chief executive of Internet startup company, Silverstream Software.

* A venture capital fund created by financier Henry Kravis to encourage economic development in New York City is investing $2 million with two troubled hospitals to help them expand a company to compete with health maintenance organizations.
* A lawsuit filed by a non-smoking flight attendant for AMR Corp's American Airlines, who came down with lung cancer, offers yet another front in the battle against cigarette companies.
* A few weeks before Hong Kong reverts to Chinese control, a phenomenon known as "tulip mania" is sweeping the colony, driving up stock of China's red-chip companies.

* A lawsuit against Silicon Graphics Inc that accused company officials of defrauding investors has been dismissed by a federal judge. The dismissal is expected to lead to the first appellate court ruling on just how far a law goes in inhibiting class-action securities lawsuits.
* The apparel industry is looking to offer more clothing to fit overweight youngsters.
* Zurich Insurance Group is close to a deal to acquire privately-held Scudder, Stevens & Clark, a money management firm, for an estimated $1.5 billion, according to sources.
